key_facts: UPDATED Saturday July 11 (T+1d, post-FP2/Q2/Sprint ahead of Sunday 30-lap main GP): (1) All-Ducati GP26 front row & Sprint sweep — Marc Marquez broke Sachsenring lap record for pole (1:19.041) and won the 15-lap Sprint wire-to-wire (+0.368s over Alex Marquez, +0.813s over Di Giannantonio); P4 Ai Ogura was +3.019s back, P5 Raul Fernandez +5.454s, P6 Jorge Martin +6.155s (qualified P9), P7 Bagnaia +7.751s (qualified P11), P8 Acosta +8.968s. Marco Bezzecchi crashed in Q2 with a displaced collarbone fracture -> OUT for Sunday (surgery in Italy). (2) MotoGP new 4m grid spacing + Sachsenring dirty-air front-tyre overheating made the Sprint a procession (Alex: nearly impossible to jump Marc off the line; Diggia: overtaking too risky when following), heavily favoring the Ducati front row (~89% combined) and polesitter Marc (0.48 -> 0.52). (3) Capped Marc at 0.52 (not 0.65+) because Marc admitted feeling uncomfortable/floating on Saturday setup (warning he needs a Warm-Up step over 30 laps), plus ~13% MotoGP crash/error risk and fierce Ducati teammates: Alex Marquez dominated FP2 (+0.321s), qualified P2 (+0.061s), pushed Marc to final lap in Sprint (+0.368s), strong 13-lap Medium pace (1:21.314) -> surged 0.06 -> 0.22; Di Giannantonio qualified P3 (+0.147s), had #1 remaining Friday Medium-tyre race pace (1:21.222 over 10 laps), and charged late in Sprint (+0.813s) -> raised 0.12 -> 0.15. (4) Ai Ogura (P5 grid, P4 Sprint, Assen winner) enters top-5 at 0.04; Raul Fernandez (P4 grid, faded to P5 +5.45s in Sprint) drops 0.12 -> 0.02; Jorge Martin (P9 grid, P6 Sprint) drops to outside tail (~0.02 alongside Bagnaia ~0.015, field ~0.015; total outside 0.05).
next_review_trigger: Resolves tomorrow (July 12, 2026) upon official MotoGP German Grand Prix main race classification.
